• If there is no visible impact, this may be a low-priority deal unless you uncover hidden value. • Explore whether the driver is growth, future readiness, compliance, differentiation, or convenience. • Reframe the offer around strategic upside instead of pain relief. • If neither pain nor upside exists, downgrade the opportunity. • Do not force urgency where the buyer does not feel any consequence.
7|Not impacted
Buyer may say, 'There is no pressing issue today.' Response: 'That is fair. Then the case has to be about strategic upside, not emergency fixing. Let us see if that exists.'
This deal needs a stronger reason to buy. Find strategic upside, leadership pressure, or future risk to create movement.
Risk: No pain often means no priority.
Ask: 'If the current state is manageable, what would make change worthwhile for you?'

• Find out whether the customer is feeling a real cost today or only exploring options. • Ask what problem is being prevented, solved, or improved through this purchase. • Probe for time loss, quality loss, support burden, learner impact, or missed business outcome. • Without visible impact, treat the deal as weakly qualified. • Clarify the pain before pushing solution detail.
